entries.explanation_en: Vて + も means “even if” or “even when” the action occurs. With a degree word such as いくら, it can mean that no matter how much or how often the action occurs, the result remains the same.

formation.explanation_en: Add も to the verb's て-form to mark the condition as concessive.

entries.title: まで (emphatic addition)
entries.reading: まで（きょうちょうてきなついか）
entries.summary_en: Adds an unexpected or extreme item, meaning “even.”
entries.explanation_en: After a noun or noun phrase, まで can extend a set to an unexpected or extreme case. In this use it emphasizes inclusion, unlike まで marking an endpoint in space, time, or extent.

formation.explanation_en: Place まで after the item emphasized as an additional or extreme case.

entries.title: ほど (degree or extent)
entries.summary_en: Marks a degree or extent, often introducing a result that reaches that degree.
entries.explanation_en: ほど follows a phrase to indicate its degree or extent. In patterns such as “so ... that,” the following clause can describe a result reached at that degree. This use is distinct from ほど after quantities to indicate an approximate amount.

formation.explanation_en: Place ほど after the phrase whose degree or extent is being indicated.

entries.title: 普通形 + かもしれない
entries.reading: ふつうけい + かもしれない
entries.summary_en: Expresses that a possibility is uncertain: “might” or “may.”
entries.explanation_en: Attach かもしれない to a plain-form predicate to present its content as possible but uncertain. With nouns and な-adjectives, だ is generally omitted before かもしれない. It expresses less certainty than a direct assertion and does not itself mark past time; the predicate conveys the time reference.

formation.form: Verb or い-adjective plain form + かもしれない
formation.explanation_en: Follows the plain form of a verb or い-adjective.

formation.form: Noun or な-adjective stem + かもしれない
formation.explanation_en: Follows a noun or な-adjective without だ.

entries.title: い形容詞のば条件形
entries.reading: いけいようしのばじょうけんけい
entries.summary_en: Forms a conditional clause with an い-adjective, meaning “if” or “when.”
entries.explanation_en: Replace the final い of an い-adjective with ければ. The result presents the adjective’s quality as a condition. The negative adjective ない follows the same pattern, becoming なければ.

formation.explanation_en: For example, 高い becomes 高ければ; ない becomes なければ.

entries.title: 動詞辞書形 + なり（即時）
entries.reading: どうしじしょけい + なり
entries.summary_en: Says that an event follows immediately after the preceding verb’s action.
entries.explanation_en: This construction presents the second event as happening as soon as the first action occurs. It has a literary or formal tone and commonly takes a verb in dictionary form before なり.

formation.explanation_en: Attach なり directly to a verb in dictionary form; the following clause gives the immediately subsequent event.

entries.title: Vてくる（変化の出現・進展）
entries.reading: てくる（へんかのしゅつげん・しんてん）
entries.summary_en: Describes an action or change emerging or developing toward a reference point, often the present.
entries.explanation_en: This use of てくる presents an action, state, or change as beginning to appear or developing toward the speaker’s reference point in time. With weather and other changes, it can convey that something has begun or is coming to be. It uses the て-form followed by くる; context distinguishes this developing sense from physical movement toward the speaker.

formation.explanation_en: Combine the verb’s て-form with くる to show emergence or development toward a reference point.

entries.title: Vない + ように (purpose or desired outcome)
entries.summary_en: States an intended outcome or purpose, often with a preceding negative form.
entries.explanation_en: ように links an action to an outcome someone aims for or takes steps to bring about. With a potential, state, or negative clause before it, it often means “so that” or “in order to.” The following clause commonly describes an action taken to achieve that outcome.

formation.explanation_en: Use the plain negative before ように to express an aim such as avoiding an outcome.

formation.form: Vる / potential form + ように
formation.explanation_en: A plain or potential form can precede ように to express an outcome being aimed for.

notes_en: Distinguish purpose ように from ようだ, which expresses resemblance or an impression.

entries.title: Clause + し (listing reasons or circumstances)
entries.summary_en: Adds a reason or circumstance to a non-exhaustive list.
entries.explanation_en: し follows a predicate and presents its clause as one reason, circumstance, or characteristic among others. It can connect multiple clauses or leave the list open, often giving a cumulative explanation.

formation.explanation_en: Attach し to a plain-form verb, adjective, or copula predicate.
Use だ before し after a noun or な-adjective predicate.

notes_en: し is a clause-linking particle here, not the verb ます-stem or the conjunctive stem.

entries.title: V / clause + ことが多い
entries.reading: どうし・せつ + ことがおおい
entries.summary_en: Says that an action or event occurs often.
entries.explanation_en: こと turns an action or clause into an event or fact, and が多い characterizes such events as frequent. The construction describes a recurring tendency rather than a single event.

formation.form: Plain-form verb or clause + ことが多い
formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the action or clause with こと, then say that such events are frequent.

notes_en: The predicate before こと is normally in plain form.

entries.title: V / clause + ことさえある
entries.reading: どうし・せつ + ことさえある
entries.summary_en: Says that an event can occur even as an extreme or unexpected case.
entries.explanation_en: こと nominalizes an action or clause; さえ adds emphatic focus, and ある presents the event as one that occurs. Together they highlight that even this event sometimes happens.

formation.form: Plain-form verb or clause + ことさえある
formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the event with こと, then use さえある to emphasize its occurrence as an extreme or unexpected case.

notes_en: Compared with こともある, ことさえある emphasizes the event as an extreme or surprising instance.

entries.title: N + ながら (concession)
entries.summary_en: Concedes a circumstance, meaning “although” or “despite being.”
entries.explanation_en: ながら can follow a noun to present that identity or circumstance as a concession to the main statement. The main clause supplies the point that holds despite the stated circumstance.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ながら directly to a noun to concede the circumstance it names.

notes_en: This concessive noun pattern is distinct from verb ます-stem + ながら, which describes simultaneous actions.

entries.title: 普通形 + なら
entries.summary_en: Takes a stated or assumed situation as the premise for what follows.
entries.explanation_en: なら frames a situation as a condition for a judgment, recommendation, or consequence. It can follow nouns, な-adjectives, and plain-form clauses. With a verb or い-adjective, it often takes up a proposition as a premise; unlike と, it does not present the result as automatic or regular.

formation.explanation_en: Attach なら directly to a noun or な-adjective.

formation.form: Verb / い-adjective plain form + なら
formation.explanation_en: Follow the plain-form proposition with なら.

entries.title: だって (emphatic addition)
entries.summary_en: Adds an item as an emphatic or unexpected example, often meaning “even.”
entries.explanation_en: だって attaches to a noun or noun phrase to include it in a set while emphasizing that it is an unexpected or noteworthy case. In this use it resembles も, often with stronger emphasis. Its other uses, including quotation-like “they say,” depend on context.

formation.explanation_en: Attach directly to the emphasized noun phrase.

entries.title: Vないことはない
entries.summary_en: Says that an action or possibility is not entirely ruled out, often as a qualified affirmation.
entries.explanation_en: A verb's plain negative form followed by ことはない presents the absence of a case in which the action is impossible. The whole pattern means that the action is possible or not impossible, often with some reservation.

formation.form: Verb plain negative + ことはない
formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the negative verb with こと and follow it with はない to express qualified possibility.

entries.title: Vる / N + たびに
entries.reading: る / めいし + たびに
entries.summary_en: Says that something occurs every time the specified event or occasion occurs.
entries.explanation_en: たびに links a recurring event or occasion to what happens on each occurrence. With verbs it follows the dictionary form; with nouns it usually follows の.

formation.explanation_en: Place たびに after a verb in dictionary form.
Use の to connect a noun to たび before に.

entries.title: 動詞の使役形
entries.summary_en: Forms a verb that presents someone as causing or allowing an action.
entries.explanation_en: The causative form indicates that a subject makes or lets another participant perform the verb's action. Whether the situation is coercive or permissive depends on context and the verb. With many transitive verbs, the person made to act is marked by に; with many intransitive verbs, を is common. Ichidan verbs add させる, godan verbs change the final う-row kana to the corresponding あ-row kana and add せる, and する and 来る have the irregular forms させる and 来させる.

formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる becomes 食べさせる.

formation.form: Godan verb: final う-row kana → あ-row kana + せる
formation.explanation_en: For example, 言う becomes 言わせる; う changes to わ before せる.

formation.form: する → させる; 来る → 来させる
formation.explanation_en: These are the irregular causative forms.

entries.title: 動詞の可能形
entries.summary_en: Expresses ability or possibility to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: The potential form presents an action as possible or within someone's ability. The person with that ability is often marked by が or は; を may be replaced by が with a potential verb. Ichidan verbs add られる, godan verbs change the final kana to the corresponding え-row kana and add る, and する and 来る have the forms できる and 来られる.

formation.explanation_en: For example, 食べる becomes 食べられる.

formation.form: Godan verb: final う-row kana → え-row kana + る
formation.explanation_en: For example, 書く becomes 書ける.

formation.form: する → できる; 来る → 来られる
formation.explanation_en: These are the potential forms of the irregular verbs.

entries.title: Vて + もらう
entries.summary_en: Presents an action as a favor or service received by the subject.
entries.explanation_en: The subject receives the benefit of another person's action. The person who performs the action is commonly marked by に. The subject's viewpoint determines who counts as receiving the benefit; the construction does not itself say that the action was requested.

formation.explanation_en: Connect the action in its て-form to もらう; conjugate もらう for the desired tense, polarity, or politeness.

entries.title: 節 + ことから
entries.summary_en: Treats a fact or circumstance as the source or basis for a conclusion.
entries.explanation_en: ことから nominalizes the preceding fact and presents it as evidence, a basis, or a cause for what follows. It often makes the inferential link explicit.

formation.explanation_en: Follow a plain-form clause with ことから; a noun or な-adjective predicate can use である before ことから.

entries.title: に (可能の主体)
entries.summary_en: Marks the person or entity for whom an action is possible or within reach.
entries.explanation_en: With potential predicates, に can identify the participant whose ability or possibility is being evaluated. は or も may follow に to mark topic or emphasis. This participant role differs from に marking an action's recipient, destination, or location.

formation.explanation_en: Place に after the person or entity whose ability is at issue.

entries.title: に (viewpoint holder with 言わせる)
entries.summary_en: Marks whose viewpoint is presented in the expression Nに言わせると.
entries.explanation_en: In the expression Nに言わせると, に marks the person whose opinion or account provides the viewpoint. The whole expression means “according to N” or “in N's view.”

formation.form: Person or group + に + 言わせると
formation.explanation_en: Place に after the viewpoint holder in this expression.

entries.title: Nに言わせると
entries.reading: めいし に いわせると
entries.summary_en: Introduces an assessment or account from someone's viewpoint: “according to N.”
entries.explanation_en: Nに言わせると presents what follows as the opinion or account of N. Though 言わせる has causative form, the expression conventionally marks a viewpoint; it does not normally assert that someone was made to speak.

formation.form: Person or group + に + 言わせると
formation.explanation_en: Follow the person whose view is being presented with に言わせると.

entries.title: から (reason or cause)
entries.summary_en: Links a stated reason or cause to a result.
entries.explanation_en: から attaches to a clause that gives the reason or cause for what follows. With a noun or な-adjective predicate, だから is used before から; with a verb or い-adjective, the plain form can be followed directly by から. It often presents the reason directly, while ので can sound more explanatory or less assertive.

formation.explanation_en: Attach から to a plain clause; use だから after a noun or な-adjective predicate.

entries.title: 普通形 + というわけではない
entries.reading: ふつうけい + というわけではない
entries.summary_en: Denies that a preceding statement is the case or the intended explanation.
entries.explanation_en: This pattern follows a plain clause and rejects it as a conclusion, interpretation, or explanation. It often means “it is not that…” or “that does not mean…,” and can soften a denial by addressing the proposed reasoning rather than simply negating a predicate.

formation.form: Plain clause + というわけではない
formation.explanation_en: Place というわけではない after a plain clause; with a noun or な-adjective predicate, use だ before という.

entries.title: ものだ (general characterization)
entries.reading: ものだ（そうごうてきなせいしつ）
entries.summary_en: Characterizes something as having a general or typical quality.
entries.explanation_en: ものだ after a noun phrase or clause presents the described quality as characteristic or general. With a noun or な-adjective, use な before もの; verbs and い-adjectives use their plain form. Its force depends on context and can be descriptive rather than a literal statement about an object.

formation.form: Noun / な-adjective + な + ものだ
formation.explanation_en: Use な to connect a noun or な-adjective to ものだ.

formation.form: Verb / い-adjective plain form + ものだ
formation.explanation_en: Attach ものだ directly to a plain-form clause.

entries.title: Potential negative + なる
entries.reading: かのうひてい + なる
entries.summary_en: Describes becoming unable to do something or a loss of ability.
entries.explanation_en: Use the plain negative of a potential verb before なる to describe a change into inability. The negative ending becomes なく before なる; inflect なる for tense and other forms as needed.

formation.form: Potential verb, plain negative + なる
formation.explanation_en: Change the negative ending ない to なく, then attach なる. The resulting expression means that the ability is lost or becomes unavailable.
The negative predicate connects to なる through its なく form.

entries.title: 少しでも (scalar “even”)
entries.summary_en: Emphasizes that even a small amount or minimal case is included.
entries.explanation_en: でも after an amount or degree phrase marks that even the stated minimum is enough to fall within the claim. It can also occur after other phrases with an inclusive or emphatic force; its interpretation depends on what it attaches to.

formation.form: Amount or degree phrase + でも
formation.explanation_en: Place でも after the phrase whose smallest or least degree is being emphasized.

entries.title: 同じ + 名詞
entries.summary_en: Uses 同じ directly before a noun to describe it as the same or identical.
entries.explanation_en: 同じ modifies a following noun directly, without な. In this use it behaves as a prenominal form, unlike ordinary な-adjectives, which take な before a noun.

formation.explanation_en: Place 同じ immediately before the noun it modifies; do not add な.

entries.title: Vるには (目的・必要条件)
entries.summary_en: Frames an action as a purpose or as a condition for what follows.
entries.explanation_en: A dictionary-form verb followed by には sets the action as the purpose or practical condition for the following statement. The following clause often says what is needed to achieve it. は gives the frame contrastive or topical focus.

formation.form: 動詞の辞書形 + には
formation.explanation_en: Attach には to a verb in dictionary form to frame the action as a purpose or condition.

entries.title: Vない + ければならない
entries.reading: ない + ければならない
entries.summary_en: Expresses that an action is necessary or required.
entries.explanation_en: Attach ければならない to the negative ない-form of a verb to say that the action must be done. The construction literally presents not doing the action as an unacceptable condition. It is a common way to express obligation or necessity.

formation.form: 動詞のない形 + ければならない
formation.explanation_en: Form the plain negative, then change ない to なければ and add ならない.

entries.title: Vて + もよい
entries.summary_en: Says that performing an action is permitted or acceptable.
entries.explanation_en: Attach もよい to a verb's て-form to state that the action is allowed. It expresses permission or acceptability, not obligation; てもいい is a common less formal variant.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb's て-form, then add もよい. The て-form connects the action to the judgment that it is acceptable.

entries.title: Vます-stem + たがる
entries.reading: ますごかん + たがる
entries.summary_en: Describes another person's outwardly apparent desire to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: Forms a verb from another person's observable behavior or expressed wishes. It commonly describes a third party; for the speaker's own desire, たい is usual. The construction reports apparent desire rather than granting direct access to another person's private thoughts.

formation.explanation_en: The desiderative たい attaches to the verb's ます-stem to express wanting to perform the action.
Replace the final い of たい with がる to describe another person's apparent desire.

entries.title: くせに
entries.summary_en: Concedes a circumstance while presenting the result as contrary to expectation, often with a critical tone.
entries.explanation_en: くせに follows a plain-form clause, noun, or な-adjective predicate and marks it as a circumstance that makes the following statement seem unexpected. It often conveys reproach or disapproval, giving it a stronger subjective tone than のに.

formation.form: Verb or い-adjective plain form + くせに
formation.explanation_en: Attach くせに directly to the plain form.

formation.form: Noun or な-adjective stem + な + くせに
formation.explanation_en: Use な before くせに after a noun or な-adjective.

entries.title: N + そのもの
entries.summary_en: Emphasizes that a person or thing is the very entity named by the noun.
entries.explanation_en: そのもの follows a noun to focus on the entity itself, often distinguishing it from an image, substitute, or interpretation of it. The noun phrase keeps its grammatical role in the sentence; そのもの adds emphasis rather than nominalizing the phrase.

formation.explanation_en: Attach そのもの directly to a noun. The resulting noun phrase can take particles such as を or が.

entries.title: 動詞辞書形 + べきだ
entries.reading: どうしじしょけい + べきだ
entries.summary_en: Says that an action is advisable, proper, or expected.
entries.explanation_en: べきだ presents the action named by a verb as what one ought to do. It often conveys a stronger sense of duty or sound judgment than a personal preference. The common form するべき may also appear as すべき.

formation.explanation_en: Attach べきだ to the dictionary form; する commonly contracts to すべきだ.

entries.title: い形容詞 + くする
entries.reading: いけいようし + くする
entries.summary_en: Describes deliberately making something take on the quality expressed by an い-adjective.
entries.explanation_en: Change the final い of an い-adjective to く and add する. The resulting transitive construction means to make something [adjective]; the thing changed is commonly marked by を. Its て-form connects the change to following material.

formation.explanation_en: Replace final い with く and add する, as in 低い → 低くする (make low).
Use the て-form of する to connect the change to following material.

entries.title: Vます-stem + すぎる
entries.reading: ますごかん + すぎる
entries.summary_en: Says that an action is done excessively or beyond an appropriate degree.
entries.explanation_en: Attach すぎる to a verb's ます-stem to describe doing too much of the action. The resulting すぎる behaves as an ichidan verb and takes ordinary verb inflections; its て-form connects the excessive action to following material.

formation.explanation_en: Attach すぎる to the ます-stem, as in 信じる → 信じすぎる (trust too much).
The resulting verb takes the ordinary て-form to connect to following material.

entries.title: 動詞の意向形 + と (意図)
entries.reading: どうしのいこうけい + と（いと）
entries.summary_en: Marks an intended action that motivates or accompanies the following action.
entries.explanation_en: Place と after a verb's volitional form to present that action as the speaker's intention or aim, often before a verb of movement or action. This use links an intended action to what is done in order to carry it out; it is distinct from と marking quoted content.

formation.explanation_en: Follow the volitional form with と to frame the action as an intention or aim.

entries.title: N + だけに (reason or fitting result)
entries.summary_en: Presents a result as fitting or especially understandable because of the stated circumstance.
entries.explanation_en: N + だけに links a circumstance to a result that is fitting, expected, or especially understandable in light of it. The result may emphasize a quality associated with the circumstance.

formation.explanation_en: Attach だけに to a noun or noun phrase that gives the reason or circumstance.

entries.title: 文末のな (observation or exclamation)
entries.summary_en: Adds a casual reflective or exclamatory tone to a statement.
entries.explanation_en: Sentence-final な can present a statement as an observation, reaction, or exclamation, often with a reflective tone. It follows a plain-style predicate. Its function differs from な used after a verb to prohibit an action.

formation.explanation_en: Place な after a plain-style statement to give it an observant or exclamatory tone.

entries.title: に決まっている
entries.summary_en: Expresses a conclusion as certain or virtually inevitable.
entries.explanation_en: Attach に決まっている to a plain-form clause or a noun phrase to present the proposition as settled or obvious. It often conveys the speaker’s strong conviction. In this use, the whole expression marks certainty; it is not the literal meaning of 決まる plus a progressive state.

formation.form: Plain-form clause or noun + に決まっている
formation.explanation_en: Follows a proposition or noun phrase; the proposition is judged certain.

entries.title: N + ばかり
entries.summary_en: Limits a phrase to what is present or done almost exclusively.
entries.explanation_en: ばかり after a noun focuses on that item or kind as making up nearly all of the relevant set, often translated as “nothing but” or “only.” With verbs it can have other uses, such as describing a just-completed action; the noun use is distinguished by what it follows.

formation.explanation_en: Follows a noun or noun phrase to express a narrow or nearly exclusive scope.

entries.title: N + に + なる (resulting status)
entries.reading: めいし + に + なる
entries.summary_en: Describes becoming or changing into a status or role named by a noun.
entries.explanation_en: Attach に to a noun before なる to present that noun as the resulting status, role, or category. The verb なる conjugates normally; the noun-plus-に pattern differs from に marking a destination or location.

formation.explanation_en: に marks the status or role reached; なる expresses the change into it.

entries.title: 数量・疑問表現 + も (negative scope)
entries.reading: すうりょう・ぎもんひょうげん + も
entries.summary_en: With a negative predicate, marks none or not even the stated amount.
entries.explanation_en: After a quantity or interrogative quantity, も can emphasize that not even that amount applies when the predicate is negative. With 一匹も, for example, the negative clause means that not even one was caught. This focused negative use differs from additive も and emphatic “even” in affirmative clauses.

formation.form: Quantity or quantity question + も + negative predicate
formation.explanation_en: The negative predicate gives も its “not even” or “none” scope.

entries.title: ているの否定形 (ていない)
entries.summary_en: Negates a ている form, denying an ongoing action or resulting state.
entries.explanation_en: Form the negative by changing いる to いない after a verb's て-form. The interpretation of ている remains context-sensitive: the negative can deny an action in progress or the state resulting from an event. It is distinct from a negative plain verb, which negates the verb without ている.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb's て-form, then the plain negative of いる. See the て-form lesson for verb-class formation.

entries.title: N のおかげで
entries.reading: めいし + のおかげで
entries.summary_en: Attributes a favorable result to a person, thing, or circumstance.
entries.explanation_en: おかげで presents the preceding person, thing, or circumstance as the reason a favorable result occurred. It often conveys gratitude or recognition of a benefit; with irony, it can point to an unwelcome result. With a noun, の links the noun to おかげ.

formation.explanation_en: Attach のおかげで to a noun. A plain-form clause can also precede おかげで to state the favorable cause.

entries.title: 普通形 + とき（時間）
entries.summary_en: Uses とき to locate an event at the time of the preceding action or state.
entries.explanation_en: A predicate in plain form can modify 時（とき）, meaning “when.” A nonpast form presents the action or state as ongoing, habitual, or upcoming at that time; a past form presents it as completed before that time. The phrase can function as a time expression within a sentence.

formation.explanation_en: Attach とき to a plain nonpast verb to refer to the time when the action occurs or is in progress.
Attach とき to a plain past verb to refer to the time after the action has occurred.

entries.title: Vます-stem + に + motion verb（目的）
entries.reading: ますごかん + に + いどうどうし
entries.summary_en: Marks an action as the purpose of going, coming, or another motion.
entries.explanation_en: The ます-stem of a verb followed by に names the purpose for which someone moves. A motion verb such as 行く, 来る, or 帰る follows. The stem is the lexical action; に links it to the purpose of the movement.

formation.form: Verb ます-stem + に + motion verb
formation.explanation_en: Use the verb’s ます-stem before に, then follow it with a motion verb such as 行く or 来る.

entries.title: Vるのが一番よい
entries.summary_en: Evaluates doing an action as the best choice.
entries.explanation_en: A plain-form verb is nominalized with の, then marked by が as the thing receiving the evaluation. 一番よい describes it as the best option. The construction can express a judgment or recommendation; よい may also appear as いい in ordinary usage.

formation.form: Verb plain form + の + が + 一番よい
formation.explanation_en: Nominalize the action with の, mark it with が, and evaluate it with 一番よい.

entries.title: N・形容詞 + 方（選択）
entries.reading: めいし・けいようし + ほう
entries.summary_en: Uses 方 to identify one side or choice, often in a comparison.
entries.explanation_en: 方 after a noun or a phrase describing a quality refers to that side, option, or member of a set. With two compared qualities, the phrase before 方 identifies the selected one. It is distinct from 方がよい, which expresses advice or preference.

formation.explanation_en: Attach の after a noun before 方 when identifying the side or option associated with that noun.
Place 方 after a phrase that specifies the selected side or option.

entries.title: N・形容詞 + にする（状態の変更）
entries.reading: めいし・けいようし + にする
entries.summary_en: Describes making something take on a named state or quality.
entries.explanation_en: Attach にする to a noun or adjective phrase to describe deliberately changing something into that status or state. With a な-adjective or noun, に marks the resulting state; with an い-adjective, use its く form before する. This use of に differs from になる, which describes a change without presenting an agent as making it happen.

formation.form: 名詞・な形容詞 + にする
formation.explanation_en: Use に after a noun or な-adjective to mark the state or status brought about by する.

formation.form: い形容詞のく形 + する
formation.explanation_en: Change final い to く before する to describe making something have that quality.

entries.title: N + ほど…ない（否定比較）
entries.summary_en: Uses a negative predicate to present a noun as an extreme in a comparison.
entries.explanation_en: ほど marks the comparison standard. With a negative predicate, the construction can say that no other thing reaches the stated degree, as in Nほど…ないものはない. A modifying clause may describe the quality being compared before the noun もの.

formation.explanation_en: Mark the comparison standard with ほど and use a negative predicate to express an extreme comparison.

formation.form: N + ほど + clause + ないものはない
formation.explanation_en: Use a negative modifying clause and ないものはない to say that nothing matches the stated extreme.

entries.title: 時間名詞の反復（逐次）
entries.reading: じかんめいしのはんぷく
entries.summary_en: Repeats a time expression to refer distributively to successive occasions.
entries.explanation_en: Repeating a time noun or time phrase can present occasions one by one over a sequence, rather than identifying two separate instances. The surrounding sentence determines whether the sense is each successive day, occasion, or interval.

formation.form: 時間表現 + 時間表現
formation.explanation_en: Repeat the time expression to refer to successive instances of that time period or occasion.

entries.title: N + たち
entries.summary_en: Forms a group or plural expression from a noun referring to a person or animate being.
entries.explanation_en: たち attaches to a noun, usually a person or other animate being, to refer to that individual together with their associated group. The group may include people or beings not explicitly named; たち is not a general plural marker for every noun.

formation.form: Person or animate-being noun + たち
formation.explanation_en: Attach たち directly to the noun; the resulting phrase refers to a group associated with that individual.

entries.title: に (basis with よる)
entries.summary_en: Marks the source or basis on which something depends or is based.
entries.explanation_en: With よる in the sense of depend on or be based on, に marks the information, circumstance, or source that provides the basis. In the expression ところによると, it marks the basis for the account that follows.

formation.explanation_en: Connect the basis to よる with に; よる then inflects as needed.

entries.title: そればかりか
entries.summary_en: Adds a further point, meaning “not only that, but also” or “moreover.”
entries.explanation_en: そればかりか connects a preceding statement with an additional fact that strengthens or extends it. It commonly introduces a further point that is surprising or more striking than what came before.

formation.explanation_en: Use before the added statement. The phrase connects that statement to the preceding discourse.

entries.title: に (event location)
entries.summary_en: Marks the place where an event occurs.
entries.explanation_en: に can locate an event or occurrence, especially with verbs describing something happening or appearing at a place. With an action performed by an agent, で more commonly marks where the action takes place.

formation.explanation_en: Place に locates the event expressed by the predicate.

entries.title: い形容詞の過去形
entries.reading: いけいようしのかこけい
entries.summary_en: Forms the plain past of an i-adjective.
entries.explanation_en: States that an i-adjective quality held in the past. Replace final い with かった; the resulting form can also modify a noun.

formation.explanation_en: Remove final い and add かった; for example, 苦しい becomes 苦しかった.

entries.title: 普通形 + だろう
entries.reading: ふつうけい + だろう
entries.summary_en: Presents a statement as probable or conjectural.
entries.explanation_en: Add だろう after a plain-form predicate to express a judgment or expectation that something is probably the case. It can also soften an assertion. With nouns and な-adjectives, だ is normally retained before だろう.

formation.explanation_en: For example, 雨が降るだろう expresses a prediction that it will probably rain.

entries.title: ものの
entries.summary_en: Connects a stated fact with a contrasting or disappointing outcome.
entries.explanation_en: Place ものの after a clause to acknowledge that it is true while presenting what follows as a contrast, limitation, or outcome short of expectation. It has a more formal tone than けれども.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ものの to a clause; nouns and な-adjectives commonly take である before it.

entries.title: Vては (反復・交替)
entries.summary_en: Pairs a recurring action or event with what repeatedly follows it, often describing an alternating cycle.
entries.explanation_en: The te-form followed by は can present an event as a repeated occasion or trigger: whenever one event occurs, another follows, and the pattern recurs. It often links alternating actions. The particle は is pronounced わ.

formation.explanation_en: Attach は to the verb's te-form. The te-form follows the regular te-form rules.

entries.title: 動詞の意向形
entries.summary_en: Forms a plain volitional verb expressing intention or invitation.
entries.explanation_en: The plain volitional form expresses the speaker’s intention or invites someone to act. It also serves as the form before とする in expressions of an attempt or imminent action.

formation.explanation_en: Change the final う-row kana to its お-row counterpart and add う: 読む → 読もう.
Replace final る with よう: 食べる → 食べよう.
Use しよう / 来よう.

entries.title: 動詞の意向形 + とする
entries.reading: どうしのいこうけい + とする
entries.summary_en: Describes an attempt or imminent action, depending on context.
entries.explanation_en: The plain volitional form followed by とする presents an action as something someone tries to do or is about to do. Context distinguishes an attempted action from one that is on the verge of occurring.

formation.explanation_en: Follow the plain volitional form with とする. The volitional form is formed according to the verb’s class.

entries.title: Vてしまう
entries.summary_en: Expresses completion or an unintended, regrettable outcome.
entries.explanation_en: Attach しまう to a verb’s て-form to present an action as completed or, depending on context, as something that happened unintentionally or with regret. The verb supplies the action; しまう adds this completion or stance.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb’s て-form before しまう.

entries.title: Vるに限る
entries.summary_en: Presents an action as the best or most advisable choice.
entries.explanation_en: Vるに限る evaluates the preceding action as the best choice in the circumstances. It often expresses a recommendation or a personal conclusion about what is preferable.

formation.explanation_en: Attach に限る to the verb’s plain nonpast form.

entries.title: に (degree with demonstratives)
entries.summary_en: Forms degree expressions such as こんなに, meaning “this much” or “so.”
entries.explanation_en: に follows expressions such as こんな, そんな, and あんな to form adverbs of degree. The resulting phrase modifies a predicate by indicating how much or to what extent.

formation.form: こんな・そんな・あんな + に
formation.explanation_en: Add に to a demonstrative expression to form a degree adverb, as in こんなに (“this much”).

entries.title: はずもない
entries.summary_en: Strongly denies that something can reasonably be expected or is possible.
entries.explanation_en: はずもない presents an outcome as having no reasonable basis or possibility. The particle も adds emphasis to the negative judgment. It can follow a plain-form clause or a noun phrase with の.

formation.explanation_en: Follow the clause being judged by はずもない; after a noun, use の before はずもない.

formation.form: Noun + の + はずもない
formation.explanation_en: Use の to connect a noun to はず, then add もない for the emphatic negative judgment.

entries.title: Vるようにする
entries.summary_en: Expresses making an effort or establishing a practice of doing something.
entries.explanation_en: Vるようにする describes a deliberate effort, decision, or practice to do the action named by the verb. The negative pattern Vないようにする expresses an effort to avoid doing it.

formation.form: Verb plain nonpast + ようにする
formation.explanation_en: Attach ようにする to a verb in plain nonpast form to describe an effort or practice.

formation.form: Verb plain negative + ようにする
formation.explanation_en: Use the plain negative before ようにする to describe an effort to avoid the action.

entries.title: 疑問詞 + ても
entries.summary_en: With an interrogative, expresses an unrestricted condition such as “wherever” or “whatever.”
entries.explanation_en: An interrogative followed by a clause ending in ても presents the result as unchanged regardless of the answer to the question word. It can express meanings such as “wherever one goes” or “whatever happens.”

formation.explanation_en: Follow an interrogative such as どこ with a clause ending in the verb’s て-form plus も; the whole expression means that the result holds regardless of the location or other queried circumstance.

entries.title: 普通形 + というより
entries.reading: ふつうけい + というより
entries.summary_en: Reframes or corrects a description by saying “rather than” or “more accurately.”
entries.explanation_en: Attach というより to a word or clause to present it as a less suitable description than what follows. It can soften a correction or replace a first impression with a more fitting characterization.

formation.form: 普通形 + というより
formation.explanation_en: Place というより after a plain-form phrase; nouns and な-adjectives may take だ before というより.

entries.title: に (additional or other scope)
entries.summary_en: With ほか, marks an additional or alternative scope, often meaning “besides” or “elsewhere.”
entries.explanation_en: ほかに can indicate an additional item or another available option. Its interpretation depends on the surrounding phrase; it does not mark a recipient simply because an English translation uses “to.”

formation.explanation_en: Attach に to ほか to frame something as additional or outside the stated set.

entries.title: で (group acting together)
entries.summary_en: Marks a group or number of participants acting together, often meaning “as a group” or “together.”
entries.explanation_en: After a noun or number phrase, で can identify the group or capacity in which an action or state applies. This use frames who acts together, unlike で marking the place of an event or the instrument used.

formation.explanation_en: Attach で to a noun or number phrase naming the group acting together.

entries.title: Vます-stem + にくい
entries.reading: ますごかん + にくい
entries.summary_en: Describes an action as difficult to perform.
entries.explanation_en: Attach にくい to a verb’s ます-stem to describe an action as difficult to do. The resulting expression behaves like an い-adjective and can be inflected for tense and polarity.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb’s ます-stem before にくい; for example, 読みます-stem + にくい gives 読みにくい, “difficult to read.”

entries.title: Vておく
entries.summary_en: Describes doing something in advance or leaving something in a resulting state.
entries.explanation_en: おく after a verb's て-form presents the action as preparation for later or as something done so that its result remains. The intended reading depends on the verb and context.

formation.explanation_en: Attach おく to the verb's て-form; おく can then take ordinary verb inflections such as the conditional ば form.

entries.title: N + として
entries.summary_en: Marks a role, capacity, or status in which someone or something acts or is considered.
entries.explanation_en: として presents a noun as the role or capacity relevant to the following action or description. It does not by itself say that the role was assigned through a decision.

formation.explanation_en: Attach として to a noun naming the relevant role or capacity.

entries.title: に (experiencer with spontaneous or passive predicates)
entries.summary_en: Marks the person who experiences a perception, feeling, or spontaneous impression.
entries.explanation_en: With predicates such as 思われる, に can mark the person to whom something seems or feels a certain way. This experiencer use differs from に marking an action's recipient, destination, or agent.

formation.explanation_en: Place に after the person experiencing the perception or impression.

entries.title: で (scope or domain)
entries.summary_en: Sets the group, field, or domain within which a statement applies.
entries.explanation_en: で can frame a group or domain as the scope for a generalization, comparison, or evaluation. This use identifies the domain of a statement rather than the physical place where a particular action occurs.

formation.explanation_en: Attach で to the noun naming the relevant group, field, or domain.

entries.title: 疑問詞 + も (全称)
entries.reading: ぎもんし + も（ぜんしょう）
entries.summary_en: With an interrogative expression, marks every member of a set when used in an affirmative clause.
entries.explanation_en: も after an interrogative such as どれ gives a universal reading, meaning that the statement applies to every possible item in the set. In negative clauses, interrogative + も commonly has a none-at-all reading instead.

formation.form: 疑問詞 + も + affirmative predicate
formation.explanation_en: Attach も to an interrogative expression; an affirmative predicate gives the reading “every” or “all.”

entries.title: 普通形 + とは限らない
entries.reading: ふつうけい + とはかぎらない
entries.summary_en: Says that a statement is not necessarily true.
entries.explanation_en: Attach とは限らない to a plain-form clause to deny that its content is certain or universally true. It often softens a generalization by leaving room for exceptions.

formation.form: plain-form clause + とは限らない
formation.explanation_en: The clause before とは限らない states what is not guaranteed to be true.

entries.title: N + のために (cause)
entries.summary_en: Connects a circumstance to an outcome it causes.
entries.explanation_en: After a noun, のために identifies that circumstance as the cause or reason for the following result. This causal use can sound more formal than ので or から and is distinct from ために expressing purpose.

formation.explanation_en: Attach のために to a noun naming the cause or circumstance.

entries.title: 普通形 + わけではない
entries.reading: ふつうけい + わけではない
entries.summary_en: Denies or qualifies an inference about a preceding statement.
entries.explanation_en: わけではない denies that a preceding statement is the case or that a conclusion drawn from it necessarily follows. It can soften a denial by limiting its scope.

formation.form: Verb or い-adjective plain form + わけではない
formation.explanation_en: Attach わけではない to a plain clause.

formation.form: Noun or な-adjective + な + わけではない
formation.explanation_en: Use な before わけではない after a noun or な-adjective predicate.

entries.title: Vるつもり
entries.summary_en: Expresses an intention or plan to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: Attach つもり to a verb in plain nonpast form to present the action as an intention or plan. The construction describes the subject’s intended action; it does not by itself say whether the plan is certain or reported.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb’s plain nonpast form before つもり.

entries.title: N + からして（判断の根拠）
entries.summary_en: Uses a feature or example as a basis for judging a larger matter.
entries.explanation_en: からして singles out a starting point or feature from which to make an inference or evaluation. It often suggests that even this one feature supports the judgment, and can also emphasize that the feature itself is revealing.

formation.explanation_en: Attach からして to a noun naming the evidence or starting point for the judgment.

entries.title: ないの連用形（なく）
entries.reading: ないのれんようけい（なく）
entries.summary_en: Changes negative ない to なく so the negated description can connect to following material.
entries.explanation_en: The i-adjective ない changes to なく before material that continues or contrasts with the negative description. The negative copula ではない likewise becomes ではなく. This form links clauses or descriptions; the negative meaning remains in force.

formation.explanation_en: Replace the final い of ない with く.

formation.form: ではない → ではなく
formation.explanation_en: Change the final ない to なく to connect a negative noun or な-adjective predicate.

entries.title: 普通形 + としても（譲歩）
entries.reading: ふつうけい + としても
entries.summary_en: Concedes a situation as a premise while saying that the following point still holds.
entries.explanation_en: としても presents a fact or supposition as something granted for the sake of the discussion, often translated as “even if” or “even granting that.” It can follow a plain predicate; nouns and な-adjectives use だとしても.

formation.explanation_en: Attach としても to a plain-form clause.

formation.form: Noun / な-adjective + だとしても
formation.explanation_en: Use だ before としても after a noun or な-adjective predicate.

entries.title: い形容詞くてたまらない
entries.reading: いけいようし + くてたまらない
entries.summary_en: Expresses a feeling or state as overwhelming or impossible to suppress.
entries.explanation_en: Attach くてたまらない to an い-adjective. With たい, the resulting たくてたまらない says that the desire to do something is overwhelming. The expression is especially common for intense feelings, sensations, and desires.

formation.form: い-adjective: い → くてたまらない
formation.explanation_en: For example, 寂しい becomes 寂しくてたまらない.

formation.form: Vます-stem + たい → たくてたまらない
formation.explanation_en: The desiderative たい behaves like an い-adjective; its て form connects to たまらない.

entries.title: Vない + なくてはならない
entries.reading: ない + なくてはならない
entries.summary_en: Expresses that an action is necessary or required.
entries.explanation_en: Change a verb to its plain negative, replace ない with なくては, and add ならない. The expression means that the action must be done. In context, なくては may appear without ならない when the obligation is understood.

formation.form: Verb plain negative: ない → なくてはならない
formation.explanation_en: For example, 行かない becomes 行かなくてはならない.

entries.title: しか + negative predicate
entries.reading: しか + ひていじゅつご
entries.summary_en: Restricts a phrase to the stated item or amount, with a negative predicate.
entries.explanation_en: しか follows the phrase being limited and requires a negative predicate. The whole clause conveys that nothing beyond the stated item or amount applies, as in これしかない, “there is only this.”

formation.explanation_en: The negative predicate gives the limiting expression its “only” sense.

entries.title: だけで (mere circumstance or means)
entries.summary_en: Says that an action or circumstance alone is enough to produce a result or judgment.
entries.explanation_en: Attach だけで to a noun, phrase, or clause to limit the relevant means or circumstance to that alone. Depending on context, it can mean “just by” or “merely because.”

formation.explanation_en: だけ limits the circumstance; で marks it as the means or basis for the result.

entries.title: あまりに
entries.summary_en: Marks an excessive degree, often translated as “far too” or “excessively.”
entries.explanation_en: あまりに modifies an adjective or other description to indicate that its degree exceeds what is usual or acceptable. It can also precede a cause or situation whose excess leads to a result.

formation.explanation_en: The following description identifies what is excessive or unusually intense.

entries.title: い形容詞 + は + ない（対比）
entries.reading: いけいようし + は + ない
entries.summary_en: Negates an i-adjective with contrastive or limiting focus on は.
entries.explanation_en: This pattern denies the stated quality while は gives the denial contrastive or limiting focus. It does not by itself assert the opposite quality.

formation.explanation_en: Use the adjective's く-form as the base for the negative.
Add は before ない to give the plain negative contrastive or limiting focus.

entries.title: N + のために（目的）
entries.summary_en: States the purpose for which an action is done.
entries.explanation_en: Attach のために to a noun naming a goal, activity, or intended beneficiary. The phrase gives the purpose motivating the following action; a cause-and-result use of ために is a different function.

formation.explanation_en: Link the noun to ため with の, then add に to mark the purpose of the following action.

entries.title: ずつ（分配）
entries.summary_en: Apportions an amount evenly across items or occasions.
entries.explanation_en: Place ずつ after an amount or measure to indicate that the amount applies to each item or is repeated in equal portions.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ずつ after the amount distributed to each item or occasion.

entries.title: ものか（反語）
entries.summary_en: Uses a rhetorical question to express strong disbelief or rejection.
entries.explanation_en: A plain-form predicate followed by ものか frames a question whose expected answer is negative. It conveys that the speaker strongly rejects or cannot believe the proposition; its force depends on context.

formation.explanation_en: Add ものか after a plain-form predicate.

entries.title: ではないか（反語・念押し）
entries.summary_en: Uses a negative question form to assert or emphasize a statement, often seeking acknowledgment or expressing surprise.
entries.explanation_en: After a plain predicate, ではないか can work as a rhetorical question that presents the statement as evident or invites the listener to recognize it. In casual speech it often appears as じゃないか. Intonation and context determine whether it sounds surprised, assertive, or like a request for agreement.

formation.explanation_en: Add the negative copular question form after a plain predicate to give the statement rhetorical or emphatic force.

entries.title: ているの縮約（てる）
entries.summary_en: Contracts ている to てる in casual speech while retaining its aspectual meaning.
entries.explanation_en: After a verb's て-form, casual speech often contracts ている to てる. The contraction keeps the ongoing-action or resulting-state meaning supplied by ている.

formation.form: Vて + いる → Vて + る
formation.explanation_en: In casual speech, omit い from いる after the verb's て-form.
Use the contracted form in casual speech without changing the aspectual meaning.

entries.title: ない → ねえ（口語縮約）
entries.reading: ない → ねえ（こうごしゅくやく）
entries.summary_en: Changes ない to the rough, casual spoken form ねえ.
entries.explanation_en: In very casual speech, ない may be pronounced and written ねえ. The change is a colloquial contraction and does not itself alter the negative meaning or the grammatical function of the form.

formation.explanation_en: Replace ない with its rough casual spoken contraction ねえ.

notes_en: Common in colloquial expressions such as じゃねえか.

entries.title: ない（存在・所有の否定）
entries.summary_en: States that something does not exist or is absent.
entries.explanation_en: ない is the negative counterpart of ある and predicates the nonexistence or absence of something. It can also appear in a clause modifying a noun, where it means that there is no person or thing matching the description.

formation.explanation_en: Use ない as a predicate to deny the existence or presence of the noun.

notes_en: Distinguish existential ない from the auxiliary ない that negates a verb.

entries.title: よ（終助詞）
entries.summary_en: Presents information as an assertion or brings it to the listener’s attention.
entries.explanation_en: Sentence-final よ marks a statement as information the speaker is asserting or supplying. Its force can range from matter-of-fact emphasis to insistence, depending on context and intonation.

formation.explanation_en: Attach よ at the end of a clause or sentence.

entries.title: ね（終助詞）
entries.summary_en: Invites acknowledgment or presents a statement as shared or confirmable.
entries.explanation_en: Sentence-final ね can seek agreement, check that the listener shares an understanding, or present an observation as something the listener can recognize. Its exact force depends on context and intonation.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ね at the end of a clause or sentence.

entries.title: ぜ（終助詞）
entries.summary_en: Adds a blunt, emphatic tone to a casual assertion or exhortation.
entries.explanation_en: Sentence-final ぜ is a strongly casual particle that presents a statement emphatically or gives an exhortation a forceful tone. It is associated with rough or masculine-coded speech and can sound brusque.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ぜ at the end of a casual clause.

entries.title: V意向形 + とはしない
entries.reading: どうしいこうけい + とはしない
entries.summary_en: Says that someone does not attempt or is unwilling to do an action.
entries.explanation_en: Follow a verb's volitional form with とはしない to emphasize that the subject makes no move to perform the action, or is unwilling to do so. The construction often conveys reluctance or refusal; context distinguishes unwillingness from simply not making an attempt.

formation.form: V意向形 + とはしない
formation.explanation_en: Use the volitional form before とはしない; the volitional names the action the subject does not attempt.

entries.title: V / N + うちに（時間内）
entries.summary_en: Places an event within a stated period, often before that period ends.
entries.explanation_en: うちに follows a time span, ongoing action, or continuing state to locate another event inside that interval. With a duration such as 一月, it means that the event occurs within that much time. It can also suggest that an opportunity may end as the situation changes.

formation.form: Time span / ongoing clause + うちに
formation.explanation_en: Attach うちに to the period or situation that bounds the time for the next event.

entries.title: い形容詞くて + も（譲歩）
entries.reading: いけいようしくて + も（じょうほ）
entries.summary_en: Says that a quality does not prevent or change the outcome.
entries.explanation_en: Change an い-adjective's final い to くて and add も. The phrase presents the quality as a conceded condition, commonly translated as “even if” or “although.” The following clause states what remains true despite that condition.

formation.form: い-adjective: い → くて + も
formation.explanation_en: 大きい becomes 大きくても. The くて form supplies the connective base for this concessive pattern.

entries.title: だ + から（理由）
entries.summary_en: Gives a reason or cause after a noun or な-adjective predicate.
entries.explanation_en: After a noun or な-adjective, だから connects the stated reason to what follows. It commonly begins a reason clause and can stand sentence-initially as “so” or “because.” Verb and い-adjective clauses use から without だ.

formation.form: N / な-adjective + だ + から
formation.explanation_en: Use だから after a noun or な-adjective predicate.

entries.title: 動詞た形 + ら（条件）
entries.reading: どうしたけい + ら（じょうけん）
entries.summary_en: Uses a verb’s た-form + ら to state a condition or an event that happens when the action is complete.
entries.explanation_en: Attach ら to a verb’s た-form to make a conditional clause. Depending on context, the clause means “if” or “when”; it can describe a hypothetical condition or an event that follows once the action occurs.

formation.explanation_en: Use the plain past form of the verb, then add ら. The past-form shape does not itself mean that the conditional event occurred.

entries.title: そのたびに
entries.summary_en: Says that an event occurs on each occasion of a previously mentioned event.
entries.explanation_en: そのたびに refers back to an event or occasion and says that something happens each time it occurs. It commonly follows a clause or refers to an event established in the surrounding context.

formation.form: Event or occasion + そのたびに
formation.explanation_en: そのたびに points back to the event or occasion and introduces what happens on each occurrence.

entries.title: Vば + いい
entries.summary_en: Says that doing an action is advisable or sufficient.
entries.explanation_en: Attach いい to a verb’s ば-conditional to present the action as a good or sufficient course. Depending on context, it can give advice (“should”) or describe what would be enough. The verb’s lexical meaning remains part of the complete expression.

formation.explanation_en: Form the conditional with the verb’s ば-form.
Add いい to express that doing the action is a good or sufficient choice.

entries.title: Vてはいられない
entries.summary_en: Says that someone cannot remain in or continue a state or action.
entries.explanation_en: Attach はいられない to a verb’s て-form to say that continuing or remaining in that state is not possible or acceptable. The expression often conveys that circumstances demand moving on or taking action.

formation.explanation_en: Use the verb’s て-form to name the action or state that cannot continue.
Use the negative potential of いる, “be able to remain,” to express inability to stay in the state.

entries.title: 節 + ため（原因・理由）
entries.reading: せつ + ため（げんいん・りゆう）
entries.summary_en: Uses a preceding clause as the cause or reason for what follows.
entries.explanation_en: A clause in plain form can precede ため to present its content as the cause or reason for a result. This use often sounds more formal or written than から.

formation.explanation_en: Attach ため to a plain-form verb, adjective, or copular clause to state its cause or reason.

entries.title: 動詞の意向形 + と思っている
entries.reading: どうしのいこうけい + とおもっている
entries.summary_en: Expresses a continuing intention or plan to perform an action.
entries.explanation_en: The volitional form is quoted with と before 思っている. The expression presents the action as an intention the subject has formed and continues to hold.

formation.form: Verb volitional form + と + 思っている
formation.explanation_en: Use the plain volitional form of the intended action, followed by quotative と and 思っている.
Forms the plain volitional base for the intended action.
